cases.on_reasoning: The system detected two identical payment instructions submitted within minutes, with the same beneficiary, amount, and value date. This pattern matches a typical ERP or system re‑send duplication rather than an intentional separate payment. No other error indicators are present.

The beneficiary bank returned AC01 indicating the account number is not found. Chinese banks recently migrated to a longer account-number format, and the 11‑digit number provided is likely an old format that is now rejected. No other clues (typo, duplicate, funds) point to alternative causes.

The payment was held due to a sanctions screening match (score 0.86) between the beneficiary name and a listed entity. No prior clearance is mentioned, so this is a new potential match requiring compliance review.

The payment was sent to the beneficiary bank on the value date but remains in a credit‑pending status, indicating the funds are likely held at the intermediary (Coromandel Clearing Bank) before reaching the beneficiary. No evidence of typo, sanctions, or duplicate issues is present.

The rejection code BE01 indicates the beneficiary name does not match the account holder name. The bank likely performs strict name matching and rejects abbreviated legal suffixes such as "Pvt Ltd". The provided name "Deccan Bio Labs Pvt Ltd" may not match the exact registered name on the account.

The payment was flagged as a duplicate (AM05) with identical details received minutes apart. A prior case (M2) for the same client showed the same pattern caused by the ERP system re‑sending the file. No other factors indicate a typo or missing data.

RR04 is a regulatory rejection code often used when required regulatory fields such as a purpose code are absent. The payment lacks any purpose or regulatory reference beyond a generic remittance note. No memory matches this pattern, so the generic rule applies.

The rejection code RC01 indicates the BIC (bank identifier) is incorrect. The most likely explanation is a one‑off data entry error in the BIC provided by the client. No memory case matches this pattern, so a general assessment is used.

The payment was rejected with AC01 indicating the beneficiary account number was not found. A similar recent case (M3/M8) involved a client-entered incorrect account number at the same bank. The provided 12‑digit number likely contains a typo or does not exist in the bank's system.
The SWIFT return code AC04 indicates the beneficiary account is closed. The beneficiary bank reported the account number as closed, matching the described error. No other patterns from memory apply.

The system detected two identical instructions (same beneficiary, amount, and close timestamps) and automatically held the second. This pattern matches known ERP duplicate re‑submission behavior. No other memory case fits the duplicate scenario.

The payment was submitted and delivered to the beneficiary bank late in the afternoon (16:08 SGT) on the same day as the value date. Indian banks often have same‑day credit cut‑offs around mid‑day, so a delivery after the cut‑off would result in the funds being credited on the next business day, matching the "credit pending" status.

The exception code AM04 indicates insufficient funds on the IDR settlement (nostro) account, while the client’s own account passed balance checks. This points to a shortfall in the bank's own funding rather than a client error. No memory case matches this scenario, so the assessment relies on standard payment knowledge.

The payment triggers a sanctions screening hit with a high match score (0.86) against a similarly named entity. A prior case (M7) with the same client, beneficiary and bank was diagnosed as a potential sanctions match. No evidence of prior false‑positive clearance exists.

The exception code AM05 indicates a duplicate instruction. The case mirrors memory M5 where Arcadia Foods had a duplicate payment to the same beneficiary and was held for the same reason. This pattern points to the client’s ERP system re‑sending the payment.

The exception code AM04 indicates insufficient funds on the IDR settlement (nostro) account, while the client’s own account passed balance checks. A similar case (M7) was diagnosed as a nostro funding shortfall.

The exception code AC01 indicates an incorrect account number. A recent similar case (M3) for the same client and beneficiary bank was caused by a client typo. The account number format appears correct (12 digits), suggesting the digits entered are wrong rather than a format change.

Tungabhadra Co-operative Bank enforces exact legal name matching (M1). The rejection code BE01 indicates the beneficiary name on the instruction differs from the account holder name, likely due to the abbreviated suffix "Pvt. Ltd." versus the bank's required "PRIVATE LIMITED". This matches a prior similar case (M8).

The exception code RC01 indicates a bank identifier error. A recent similar case (M5) involved the same client and beneficiary bank where a BIC typo caused rejection. The pattern matches, suggesting a data‑entry mistake in the BIC or bank identifier.

Manila Bay Savings Bank enforces exact legal name matching. The rejection code BE01 indicates the beneficiary name on the payment does not exactly match the account holder name, which is typical of a legal suffix mismatch rather than a simple typo.

The payment was submitted at 14:52 SGT, after Golconda Commercial Bank's same‑day cut‑off of 12:00 IST (14:30 SGT). The bank therefore processes the credit on the next business day, so the beneficiary will not see funds on the requested value date of 2 Sep.

The payment is a USD trade transfer above the threshold and the remittance information only contains a generic note without a required regulatory purpose code. Victoria Harbour Bank often enforces purpose codes for such payments, and the RR04 regulatory reject aligns with a missing reporting field.

The hold code AM05 indicates a duplicate detection. The pattern (identical instruction received minutes apart) matches memory M3 where Arcadia Foods' ERP re‑sent a weekend batch, causing a duplicate that was cancelled. No other evidence points to a different cause.

The screening hit (0.86) mirrors earlier holds on payments to Desert Star General Trading LLC that were cleared by Compliance as a false positive (M4, M6). The same beneficiary, bank, and match score indicate this is the same issue, not a new sanction risk.

The payment was rejected with AC01 due to an invalid IBAN check digit, which typically indicates a data entry error. A similar past case (M3) was caused by a client typo leading to AC01. No evidence of format changes or other issues applies here.

RC01 indicates a bank identifier error. A prior case (M3) with the same client and beneficiary bank was caused by an incorrect BIC, matching the current symptoms. No other memory suggests a routing change or cut‑off issue, so a client typo is most likely.

The AC01 reject indicates the account number is not recognized. A prior case (M5) for Sunrise Textiles with the same beneficiary bank was caused by an outdated account format, and another case (M6) shows Pearl Delta migrated to a 15‑digit format. The 12‑digit number supplied is likely no longer valid.

The payment was sent well before typical GBP cut‑offs, and the beneficiary account format looks correct. The only abnormality is the status from Albion Clearing Bank indicating a pending compliance check, which points to the funds being held at the intermediary. No other clues (sanctions, missing invoice, name mismatch) apply.

The AM04 hold code explicitly means the client’s debit account balance check failed, indicating insufficient funds. The message confirms the client balance check failed. A prior case (M4) with the same client and AM04 code was also due to insufficient funds, reinforcing this diagnosis.

RR04 is a regulatory rejection code commonly used for missing or incorrect purpose codes on INR outbound payments. The remittance information only contains "Services" and no purpose code was supplied. No memory case matches this exact scenario, so we rely on general knowledge.

Tungabhadra Co-operative Bank enforces exact legal name matching and rejects abbreviations like 'Pvt Ltd'. The beneficiary name used ('Deccan Bio Labs Pvt Ltd') does not match the registered 'DECCAN BIO LABS PRIVATE LIMITED', which matches prior rejections (M3, M6, M8).

The payment was submitted at 15:40 SGT and arrived at Golconda Commercial Bank at 15:44 SGT, both after the bank’s same‑day cut‑off of 14:30 SGT. Golconda credits such payments on the next business day, so the beneficiary will not see the funds on the intended value date.

The payment was held with AM05 duplicate code after two identical instructions arrived minutes apart. The client and beneficiary match several past cases (M1,M2,M3,M5,M8) where the ERP system re‑sent the same file, leading to the same error. This pattern strongly points to an ERP‑generated duplicate.

RC01 indicates the BIC (bank identifier) is incorrect, which points to a data‑entry error on the client side. No memory case matches this pattern, so we rely on standard knowledge that such rejections are caused by typos in BIC/IBAN details.

Victoria Harbour Bank rejects trade payments over USD 10,000 if the remittance lacks an invoice number, returning RR04. The payment of USD 16,750 only contains "Components" with no invoice reference, matching past cases M1, M3 and the bank policy noted in M7. This pattern fits the current rejection.

The payment triggered a sanctions screening hit with a high match score (0.91) and there is no prior clearance or false‑positive record for this beneficiary in our memory. Therefore it must be treated as a new potential match and escalated to Compliance.

The payment was sent via Coromandel Clearing Bank and the last update shows a pending status at the intermediary, indicating the funds have not yet been released. A similar non‑receipt claim (M8) involving the same beneficiary and intermediary was also due to an intermediary hold. No rejection code or missing purpose code was reported, so the delay is most likely at the correspondent bank.

The payment matches two prior cases (M3, M7) where the same client, beneficiary, and 0.86 match score were cleared as a known false positive. The desk has a clearance reference (CLR-2026-0819-07) for this beneficiary, indicating this is not a new sanctions issue.

The payment was flagged by AM05 duplicate detection because two instructions with identical beneficiary and amount were received within an hour. A past case (M1) with the same bank and duplicate hold was resolved after the client confirmed the payments were for separate invoices, indicating this situation requires verification rather than assuming an ERP error.

Pearl Delta Commercial Bank recently switched from a 12‑digit to a 15‑digit account‑number format. The supplied 12‑digit number (********5527) matches the old format, triggering AC01. This matches the pattern in memory M8 where the same bank’s format change caused a rejection.

The RC01 "Bank identifier incorrect" was returned by the intermediary, and the payment used Atlantic Clearing Bank, which past cases (M3, M4) show is an outdated correspondent for Nordkyst Bank. The same client and beneficiary experienced rejections for the same reason when the routing was not updated, indicating a routing change is the cause.

The duplicate check flagged two identical instructions (06:14 and 06:43) with the same beneficiary, amount and value date, which matches previous ARCadia Foods duplicate cases (M4, M5, M8). The reason code AM05 also indicates an ERP‑generated duplicate. No other error patterns apply.

The SWIFT return code AC04 explicitly means the beneficiary account is closed. A previous desk case (M1) with the same code was diagnosed as a closed account, matching the current facts. No other error patterns (typo, format change, sanctions, etc.) apply.

The payment reached Golconda Commercial Bank at 15:18 SGT, after the bank’s same‑day inbound cut‑off, so the credit is scheduled for the next business day. This mirrors past cases (M4, M3) where Vantage Analytics’ INR transfers to the same beneficiary were delayed for the same reason.

AC01 indicates the account number was not recognised. A prior case (M3) with the same error code was caused by a data‑entry typo, and there is no indication of a format change or other issue. The most likely explanation is an incorrect account number entered by the client.

Tungabhadra Co-operative Bank rejects payments where the beneficiary name does not exactly match the legal name on the account. The submitted name uses the abbreviation “Pvt Ltd”, which the bank does not accept, leading to BE01. Past case M1 showed the same client/beneficiary and BE01 rejection, and M6 documents the bank’s exact‑match policy.

RR04 is a regulatory reject code used by Victoria Harbour Bank for trade payments lacking required invoice details. The same client and beneficiary were previously rejected for the identical reason (M1). The remittance info only contains a generic note, confirming the missing invoice reference.

The AC01 rejection means the account number was not found. Past memory (M2) shows Pearl Delta Commercial Bank migrated to a 15‑digit format, requiring a branch‑code prefix. The client supplied a 12‑digit number, matching the old format, so the bank rejects it. This pattern matches the current case.

The payment matches several prior cases (M1‑M3) where the same client, beneficiary and 0.86 match score triggered a hold. Memory M4 shows the same hit was cleared as a false positive by Compliance (CLR‑2026‑0819‑07). The pattern indicates this is the same known false positive.
